title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy: Loss Settlement Conditions
content:
## Section I Conditions — Loss Settlement

These conditions govern how a covered loss under the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy is paid. Each package applies them with its own personal property settlement basis (actual cash value or replacement cost), its own no-holdback threshold and its own deductible waiver threshold, as shown on the package schedule.

**A. Claim number.** A payment is issued only on a claim number opened by first notice of loss. The claim file must show the first-notice entry for that claim number before any payment is issued on it.

**B. Settlement elements.** Each covered coverage part and property class of a claim is settled from its replacement-cost value, its depreciation and the deductible.

**C. Deductible — clause no longer in force.** The following clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current settlement basis: "One deductible applies per occurrence: for a wind or hail loss it is the larger of the wind and hail deductible percentage applied to Coverage A and the package's wind and hail deductible minimum, and for every other cause of loss it is the all-other-perils deductible; it is absorbed first by the dwelling, then by other structures, then by personal property, until used up."

**D. Deductible waiver.** When the total covered replacement-cost value of the occurrence is at or above the package's deductible waiver threshold, on a package whose threshold is above 0, no deductible applies.

**E. Below the deductible.** When the covered replacement-cost value of a coverage part does not exceed the deductible left for it to absorb, that part is denied as below the deductible.

**F. Dwelling, other structures and replacement-cost contents — clause no longer in force.** The following clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current settlement basis: "For the dwelling and other structures, and for personal property on a replacement-cost package, when the replacement-cost value is at or below the no-holdback threshold the payment is a full replacement-cost payment, equal to the replacement-cost value less the deductible absorbed; otherwise the first payment is an actual-cash-value initial payment, equal to the replacement-cost value less depreciation less the deductible absorbed, and the depreciation is withheld in one holdback entry."

**G. Personal property on an actual-cash-value package.** For personal property on a package whose personal property settles at actual cash value, the payment is an actual-cash-value final payment, equal to the replacement-cost value less depreciation less the deductible absorbed, and nothing is withheld.

**H. Limits.** The replacement-cost value is capped at what remains of the part's limit:

| Coverage part or class | Limit that caps the replacement-cost value |
|---|---|
| Dwelling | Coverage A, plus the package's extended replacement cost percentage of Coverage A on a total loss |
| Other structures | The package's other structures percentage of Coverage A |
| Personal property | The personal property limit on the declarations |
| Theft of jewelry, watches and furs | The package's jewelry theft limit |
| Theft of firearms | The package's firearms theft limit |
| Money, bank notes and coins | The package's money limit |

**I. Loss of use.** Loss of use is reimbursed as incurred, with no deductible, up to the package's loss of use percentage of Coverage A, and for no longer than the package's loss of use maximum months after the date of loss.

**J. Payee.** A dwelling or other structures payment at or above the package's mortgagee co-payee threshold is payable to the insured and the mortgagee when a mortgagee is on file. Every other payment is payable to the insured.

**K. Roof and water.** Roof surfacing of a wind or hail claim is settled under the HomeGuard roof surfacing settlement rules, and water losses under the HomeGuard water damage limitations, before this arithmetic is applied.

## Applying the conditions — hypothetical figures

All amounts below are hypothetical inputs chosen for illustration.

- **Waiver (D).** On a package with a waiver threshold of 50000 USD, an occurrence with total covered replacement-cost value of 50000 USD carries no deductible; one of 49999.99 USD does not reach the threshold. On a package whose threshold is 0, the waiver never applies.
- **Below the deductible (E).** With 1000 USD of deductible left for a part: covered replacement-cost value of 800 USD, denied; 1000 USD, denied, because it does not exceed the deductible left; 1000.01 USD, not denied under this condition.
- **Actual-cash-value final payment (G).** Personal property replacement-cost value 6000 USD, depreciation 1500 USD, deductible absorbed 1000 USD: the payment is 6000 less 1500 less 1000, that is 3500 USD, and nothing is withheld.
- **Payee (J).** With a co-payee threshold of 2500 USD and a mortgagee on file: a dwelling payment of 2500 USD is payable to the insured and the mortgagee; a dwelling payment of 2499.99 USD is payable to the insured; a personal property payment of any amount is payable to the insured.

superseded_clauses: For dwelling and other_structures, and for personal_property on a replacement_cost tier, when RC is at or below rc_no_holdback_threshold the payment is replacement_cost_full, equal to RC minus the deductible absorbed; otherwise the first payment is acv_initial, equal to RC minus depreciation minus the deductible absorbed, and the depreciation is withheld in one home_holdback_withheld entry.

One deductible applies per occurrence: for peril wind_hail it is the larger of wind_hail_deductible_pct of Coverage A and wind_hail_deductible_minimum, and for every other peril it is the aop_deductible; it is absorbed first by dwelling, then other_structures, then personal_property, until used up.
